sections.title: CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: EARLY MORNING WV IMAGERY CLEARLY DEPICTS A SHORT-WAVE TROUGH OVER THE GREAT BASIN EJECTING NEWD TOWARD WY IN LINE WITH LATEST SHORT-RANGE MODEL GUIDANCE. STRONGER FLOW IN ASSOCIATION WITH THIS FEATURE WILL SPREAD ACROSS THE NRN HIGH PLAINS DURING THE DAY ALONG WITH WEAK HEIGHT FALLS. ALTHOUGH THIS SHORT-WAVE IS EXPECTED TO LIFT MORE NLY WITH TIME IT APPEARS THE SRN-MOST INFLUENCE WILL CLIP NERN CO AROUND PEAK HEATING ENHANCING THE LIKELIHOOD FOR ANOTHER BOUT OF SIGNIFICANT TSTM ACTIVITY BY MID-LATE AFTERNOON. LATEST MODEL GUIDANCE INSISTS SFC CYCLONE WILL HOLD TIGHT AGAINST THE HIGHER TERRAIN OF THE FRONT RANGE OF CO DURING THE PERIOD. THIS WILL ENSURE MOIST UPSLOPE FLOW IS MAINTAINED WHICH SHOULD ENCOURAGE CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT BETWEEN 21-00Z. FORECAST SOUNDINGS FAVOR SUPERCELL STRUCTURES AS DEEP LAYER SHEAR SHOULD BE ON THE ORDER OF 30-35KT WITH SUBSTANTIAL TURNING NOTED THROUGH 9KM. STORMS THAT INITIATE ACROSS CO INTO THE NEB PANHANDLE ARE EXPECTED TO PRODUCE HAIL AS THEY MATURE AND SPREAD SEWD AT ROUGHLY 10KT. ADDITIONALLY...A FEW TORNADOES CAN ALSO BE EXPECTED AS CLOUD BASES WILL BE SEASONABLY LOW WITH SFC TEMP/DEW POINT SPREADS OF ROUGHLY 20F.

sections.title: DAKOTAS
sections.text: SFC FRONT IS EXPECTED TO PROGRESS INTO THE CNTRL DAKOTAS BY 18Z WITH SUBSTANTIAL LOW LEVEL HEATING EXPECTED ALONG/AHEAD OF THE WIND SHIFT. THIS BOUNDARY WILL ADVANCE WELL AHEAD OF THE STRONGER FLOW ALOFT AND RESULTANT DEEP LAYER SHEAR IS EXPECTED TO LAG CONSIDERABLY ACROSS ERN MT...POSSIBLY SPREADING INTO THE WRN DAKOTAS LATE. ANY STORMS THAT FORM ALONG THE COLD FRONT WILL DO SO WITHIN AN ENVIRONMENT OF STEEP LAPSE RATES THAT SHOULD FAVOR PULSE-MULTICELL UPDRAFTS. FOR THIS REASON WILL MAINTAIN 5% SEVERE PROBS FOR WIND/HAIL ACROSS THIS REGION.

sections.title: CNTRL TX
sections.text: NNWLY MID LEVEL FLOW ON THE ORDER OF 30-40KT WILL CONTINUE ACROSS NWRN TX INTO CNTRL TX ALONG BACK SIDE OF SLOW MOVING UPPER LOW AS IT DRIFTS SEWD. THIS FLOW COULD ENHANCE THE POTENTIAL FOR UPDRAFTS TO ORGANIZE ALONG LOW LEVEL CONFLUENCE ZONE THAT WILL ORIENT ITSELF ACROSS CNTRL TX DURING THE AFTERNOON HOURS. AT THIS TIME WILL MAINTAIN 5% SEVERE PROBS ACROSS THIS REGION BUT IF IT APPEARS LOW LEVEL CONVERGENCE CAN FOCUS MORE CONCENTRATED STORMS ACROSS THIS REGION THERE MAY BE A NEED FOR ENHANCED SEVERE PROBS TO ACCOUNT FOR WIND/HAIL THREAT...PRIMARILY DURING THE AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING HOURS.

sections.title: PA/NJ
sections.text: VERY COLD MID LEVEL TEMPERATURES...MINUS 18-20C AT 500 MB...WILL EXTEND ACROSS PA/NJ DURING THE DAY. IT APPEARS STRONG BOUNDARY LAYER HEATING WILL CONTRIBUTE TO STEEP LOW LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND CONVECTIVE TEMPERATURES WILL LIKELY BE REACHED AS READINGS RISE INTO THE UPPER 60S/LOWER 70S BY 18Z. ALTHOUGH LOW LEVEL MOISTURE IS NOT THAT SIGNIFICANT...OR DEEP LAYER SHEAR...IT WOULD SEEM PLAUSIBLE THAT ROBUST UPDRAFTS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL COULD DEVELOP DURING THE HEAT OF THE DAY. ACTIVITY SHOULD SPREAD/DEVELOP SWD AT ROUGHLY 10KT WITH WEAKENING EXPECTED WITH LOSS OF DAYTIME HEATING. ..DARROW/LEITMAN.. 06/07/2012

sections.title: TX
sections.text: A WEAK AND CONVECTIVELY AIDED UPPER LOW PERSISTS OVER NORTH TX. RATHER STRONG MID LEVEL WINDS IN SOUTHWEST PERIPHERY OF THE LOW...COUPLED WITH STRONG HEATING AND AMPLE CAPE...WILL PROMOTE THE DEVELOPMENT OF SCATTERED STRONG STORMS THIS AFTERNOON. STEEP LOW LEVEL LAPSE RATES SUGGEST LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS ARE THE MAIN THREAT.

sections.title: PA/WV/MD
sections.text: MID/UPPER LEVEL CYCLONIC FLOW REMAINS OVER THE NORTHEAST STATES TODAY...WITH A WEAK SHORTWAVE TROUGH MOVING SOUTHWARD ACROSS ONTARIO/LOWER MI. LIFT AHEAD OF THIS FEATURE WILL HELP TO INITIATE SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS BY EARLY AFTERNOON OVER PARTS OF PA. COOL TEMPERATURES ALOFT /-18 AT 500MB/ WILL PROMOTE A RISK OF HAIL IN THE STRONGER STORMS. ACTIVITY WILL SAG SOUTHWARD INTO MD/WV/VA DURING THE AFTERNOON AND EARLY EVENING BEFORE DIURNAL COOLING WEAKENS THE STORMS. ..HART/MOSIER.. 06/07/2012

sections.title: NRN PLAINS INTO CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: WATER VAPOR IMAGERY SHOWS A PRIMARY SHORT WAVE TROUGH MOVING ENEWD FROM CENTRAL MT SWD INTO WRN WY...WITH A SRN STREAM SHORT WAVE TROUGH MOVING INTO THE CENTRAL ROCKIES ATTM. THESE FEATURES ARE EXPECTED TO INFLUENCE CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING...WITH SEVERAL STRONG THUNDERSTORMS ALREADY OCCURRING OVER PARTS OF NERN WY IN ADVANCE OF THE NRN TROUGH. AT THE SURFACE...THE PATTERN IS EXPECTED TO CHANGE LITTLE WITH A LOW OVER THE CENTRAL DAKOTAS BORDER REGION...AND A WEAK FRONT TRAILING SSWWD ACROSS THE NEB PANHANDLE INTO CENTRAL CO. A DENVER CYCLONE/CONVERGENCE ZONE IS APPARENT IN THE SURFACE DATA AND THIS MAY PERSIST THROUGH MUCH OF THE AFTERNOON. THESE FEATURES ARE EXPECTED TO FOCUS CONVECTIVE STORMS THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING. VISIBLE IMAGERY INDICATES SEVERAL REGIONS OF THICKER CLOUD COVER FROM NERN CO NNEWD INTO THE WRN DAKOTAS...AND THESE WILL MODULATE DIABATIC HEATING AND SUBSEQUENT DESTABILIZATION DURING THE AFTERNOON. LOW LEVEL MOISTURE WITH SURFACE DEW POINTS GENERALLY IN THE 50S IS EXPECTED TO PERSIST ALONG/AHEAD OF THE FRONTAL ZONE...WITH LARGER INSTABILITY /MLCAPE OF 1000-2000 J PER KG/ EXPECTED WITHIN REGIONS WHERE REDUCED CLOUD COVER AND GREATER HEAT

sections.title: MIDDLE ATLANTIC REGION
sections.text: A WEAK SHORT WAVE TROUGH ASSOCIATED WITH COOL MID LEVEL TEMPERATURES /-16 TO -18C AT 500MB/ IS FORECAST TO MOVE SEWD ACROSS THE AREA TODAY. RELATIVELY CLEAR SKIES WILL PROMOTE DIURNAL HEATING THIS AFTERNOON...AND WITH SURFACE DEW POINTS IN THE 50S...THE AIR MASS WILL BECOME MODESTLY UNSTABLE WITH MLCAPE OF 500-750 J/KG. RELATIVELY LOW TOPPED THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING AND SEVERAL MAY PRODUCE MARGINAL HAIL AND GUSTY WINDS.

sections.title: SOUTH TEXAS
sections.text: A WEAK AND CONVECTIVELY AIDED UPPER LOW PERSISTS OVER NORTH TX. RATHER STRONG MID LEVEL WINDS IN SOUTHWEST PERIPHERY OF THE LOW...COUPLED WITH STRONG HEATING AND AMPLE CAPE...WILL PROMOTE THE DEVELOPMENT OF SCATTERED STRONG STORMS THIS AFTERNOON. THIS IS MOST LIKELY TO OCCUR ALONG AND SOUTH OF A COMPOSITE BOUNDARY EVIDENT IN VISIBLE IMAGERY ALONG A RKP-HDO-ECY LINE. THE WRN PART OF THIS BOUNDARY IS MOVING SWD IN RESPONSE TO REINFORCING OUTFLOW FROM STORMS OVER CENTRAL TX. ..WEISS/COHEN.. 06/07/2012

sections.title: CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: SCATTERED SUPERCELLS HAVE MATURED ACROSS THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS FROM SERN WY/NEB PANHANDLE...SWD ACROSS PORTIONS OF ERN CO. THIS ACTIVITY WILL REMAIN CONCENTRATED ACROSS UPSLOPE REGIONS OF THIS TRI-STATE REGION WITH ADDITIONAL DEVELOPMENT EXPECTED...ALONG WITH STORM MERGERS OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. 00Z SOUNDING FROM DNR EXHIBITS VERY STEEP LAPSE RATES THROUGH 9KM WITH SBCAPE IN EXCESS OF 2500 J/KG. IN THE ABSENCE OF EXTENSIVE CONVECTIVE OVERTURNING IT APPEARS ONGOING CONVECTION SHOULD LINGER WELL INTO THE LATE EVENING HOURS AS LLJ IS EXPECTED TO INCREASE ACROSS NWRN KS INTO SWRN NEB AFTER DARK. WHILE LARGE HAIL IS EXPECTED TO BE THE MAIN SEVERE THREAT...AT TIMES EXCEEDING GOLF BALL SIZE WITH STRONGER CORES....ISOLATED TORNADOES REMAIN POSSIBLE...ESPECIALLY FOR THE NEXT FEW HOURS.

sections.title: DAKOTAS
sections.text: TWO MAIN CLUSTERS OF CONVECTION ARE PROGRESSING ACROSS THE DAKOTAS THIS EVENING IMMEDIATELY AHEAD OF EJECTING SHORT-WAVE TROUGH. THE LEAD ACTIVITY APPEARS TO BE DRIVEN IN PART BY WARM ADVECTION AND WILL SOON LIFT INTO SRN MB AND EXTREME NWRN MN. ANOTHER ORGANIZED MCS HAS EVOLVED OVER WRN SD WHICH WILL PROGRESS EAST OF THE INSTABILITY AXIS SHORTLY. INTENSITY WITH THIS ACTIVITY SHOULD GRADUALLY WANE OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. ISOLATED WIND/HAIL MAY ACCOMPANY EACH OF THESE COMPLEXES BUT OVERALL TRENDS ARE DECREASING.

sections.title: MIDDLE/UPPER TX COAST
sections.text: STRONG/SEVERE TSTMS HAVE ORGANIZED ACROSS THE COAST PLAINS OF TX FROM NEAR HOU...SWWD TO NORTH OF CRP. THIS ACTIVITY MAY BE PARTLY ENHANCED BY SEA BREEZE CONVERGENCE SUGGESTING THAT INTENSITIES ARE LIKELY AT THEIR GREATEST LEVELS. FOR THIS REASON WILL MAINTAIN 5% SEVERE PROBS FOR HAIL/WIND FOR THE NEXT FEW HOURS. ..DARROW.. 06/08/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: TIMING IS STILL SOMEWHAT UNCERTAIN...BUT A WW WILL LIKELY BE NEEDED BY 20-21Z...IF NOT BEFORE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: ISOLATED TO WIDELY SCATTERED STORMS HAVE ALREADY INITIATED OFF THE MEDICINE BOW MOUNTAINS IN RESPONSE TO BOUNDARY LAYER DESTABILIZATION AND OROGRAPHIC FORCING. THIS PROBABLY HAS BEEN AIDED BY FORCING FOR UPWARD VERTICAL MOTION ASSOCIATED WITH LARGER SCALE MID/UPPER TROUGHING LIFTING OUT OF THE EASTERN GREAT BASIN...WHICH IS EXPECTED TO CONTRIBUTE TO ADDITIONAL INCREASING STORM DEVELOPMENT NEAR/NORTH AND EAST OF THE LARAMIE MOUNTAINS BY THE 18-20Z. MODERATELY SHEARED DEEP LAYER MEAN FLOW IS STILL SOUTHERLY...BUT EXPECTED TO VEER WITH TIME WHICH WILL CONTRIBUTE TO EASTWARD PROPAGATION OF STORMS THROUGH THE HIGH PLAINS...WHERE CONVECTIVE INHIBITION WILL CONTINUE TO WEAKEN...AS MIXED LAYER CAPE INCREASES IN EXCESS OF 1500 J/KG. LARGE HAIL APPEARS THE PRIMARY SEVERE THREAT...PARTICULARLY WITH INITIAL ACTIVITY NEAR THE HIGHER TERRAIN. HOWEVER...AS ACTIVITY STRENGTHENS AND DEVELOPS EASTWARD...A FEW SUPERCELLS ARE EXPECTED...ALONG WITH THE RISK FOR LOCALLY DAMAGING WIND GUSTS...PERHAPS AN ISOLATED TORNADO OR TWO.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A THREAT FOR SVR THUNDERSTORMS MAY INCREASE THIS AFTERNOON ACROSS N-CNTRL/CNTRL/S-CNTRL ND. TRENDS WILL CONTINUE TO BE MONITORED...AND A WW MAY BE NEEDED THIS AFTERNOON.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST SFC MESOANALYSIS DEPICTS A STATIONARY FRONT EXTENDING N-S OVER THE WRN HALF OF ND. ALONG THIS FRONT LIES A SFC LOW SW OF BISMARCK...WITH A WARM FRONT EXTENDING E OF THE LOW. LOW-LEVEL MASS FLUX INTO WRN ND ON THE NOSE OF A MODEST LOW-LEVEL JET CONTINUES SUPPORTING SCATTERED ELEVATED CONVECTION WEST OF THE STATIONARY FRONT. THIS ACTIVITY MAY POSE A HAIL THREAT INTO THE AFTERNOON AS INFLOW INTO THIS ACTIVITY DESTABILIZES. EAST OF THE STATIONARY FRONT...INSOLATION/DIBABATIC HEATING ON EITHER SIDE OF THE WARM FRONT MAY AID IN ITS NWD MOTION WITH MLCAPE VALUES INCREASING TO 1000-2000 J/KG AS SFC DEWPOINTS HOLD IN THE LOWER 60S. THIS MAY SUPPORT SFC-BASED CONVECTIVE INITIATION EAST OF THE STATIONARY FRONT BY LATE AFTERNOON...POSSIBLY EVOLVING FROM THE WNW-ESE-ORIENTED ARC OF ELEVATED CONVECTION CURRENTLY CROSSING THE STATIONARY FRONT NEAR THE LOW. HOWEVER...IT MAY TAKE AT LEAST A FEW HOURS FOR STRONG ANTECEDENT SFC-BASED INHIBITION TO ERODE PER A MODIFIED 12Z BISMARCK SOUNDING...WITH AROUND 100 J/KG OF SBCINH REMAINING AS OF EARLY AFTERNOON. A ZONE OF ENHANCED SLY MID-LEVEL FLOW OVER THE ERN PERIPHERY OF A WRN CONUS LONGWAVE TROUGH WILL BE ASSOCIATED WITH 25-35 KT OF EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR...WHICH MAY SUPPORT OCCASIONALLY ORGANIZED STORM STRUCTURES AND PERHAPS TRANSIENT SUPERCELLS WITH ANY SFC-BASED CONVECTION. SVR HAIL/WIND WILL BE THE MAIN CONCERNS WITH THIS ACTIVITY...THOUGH A WEAK/BRIEF TORNADO CANNOT BE RULED OUT NEAR THE AFOREMENTIONED SFC BOUNDARIES/LOW.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: IT IS NOT CERTAIN THAT A NEW WW WILL BE NEEDED ACROSS WESTERN SOUTH DAKOTA...BUT TRENDS NORTH/NORTHEAST OF WW 362 WILL CONTINUE TO BE MONITORED FOR THE POSSIBILITY OF AN INCREASING SEVERE THREAT LATE THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: IT APPEARS THAT THE PRIMARY AREA OF MID-LEVEL FORCING FOR UPWARD VERTICAL MOTION...ASSOCIATED WITH THE SHORT WAVE TROUGH LIFTING NORTH NORTHEASTWARD OUT THE GREAT BASIN...IS IN THE PROCESS OF SHIFTING INTO WESTERN SOUTH DAKOTA AND ADJACENT AREAS OF THE HIGH PLAINS. HOWEVER...LATEST OBJECTIVE ANALYSES SUGGEST THAT STRONGEST DESTABILIZATION REMAINS FOCUSED TO THE LEE OF THE FRONT RANGE...WHERE SOUTHERLY NEAR SURFACE FLOW IS MAINTAINING RELATIVELY HIGH SURFACE DEW POINTS...AND THE BOUNDARY LAYER CONTINUES TO WARM WITH INSOLATION. SCATTERED NEW CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT PERSISTS ACROSS THE HIGHER TERRAIN...WHICH SHOULD CONTINUE TO INTENSIFY THROUGH 22-00Z...WHILE SLOWLY PROPAGATING INTO THE HIGH PLAINS. SUPERCELLS WITH LARGE HAIL...LOCALLY DAMAGING WIND GUSTS...AND AN ISOLATED TORNADO OR TWO REMAINS POSSIBLE. ..KERR.. 06/07/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLD LARGE HAIL AND STRONG-SEVERE WIND GUSTS WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE FOR THE NEXT FEW HOURS WITH SCTD TSTM ACTIVITY OVER SWRN AND W-CNTRL SD.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RECENT SURFACE-RADAR MESOANALYSIS PLACES A LOW NEAR PHP WITH A RAPIDLY SURGING GUST FRONT --EFFECTIVE FRONT-- SITUATED FROM NEAR THE LOW SWWD INTO FAR SWRN SD. ALONG AND AHEAD OF THE BOUNDARY...THE AIRMASS HAS DESTABILIZED AS TEMPS WARMED INTO THE UPPER 80S AND DEWPOINTS IN THE MID 50S. DEEP LAYER SHEAR /0-6 KM GENERALLY BELOW 30 KTS/ DECREASES WITH EWD EXTENT ACROSS THE DISCUSSION AREA AND THIS WILL TEND TO LIMIT OVERALL STORM ORGANIZATION POTENTIAL. ALTHOUGH SHORT-TERM CONVECTIVE-THERMODYNAMIC TRENDS WOULD SUGGEST A BRIEF 1-2 HR PERIOD FOR SEVERE HAIL/WIND PRIOR TO SUBSTANTIAL CONVECTIVE OVERTURNING...APPRECIABLE LARGE SCALE FORCING FOR ASCENT VIA A SHORTWAVE TROUGH --MOVING ACROSS NERN WY/SERN MT/WRN DAKOTAS-- WILL ACT TO AT LEAST SUPPORT SOME RISK FOR SEVERE INTO THE EARLY EVENING HOURS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE POTENTIAL FOR SUPERCELLS WITH TORNADOES AND VERY LARGE HAIL /EXCEEDING 2 INCH DIAMETER/ WILL PERSIST INTO THE EVENING ACROSS THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS REGION FROM SERN WY AND NEB PANHANDLE SWD THROUGH NORTH CENTRAL/NERN TO PARTS OF EAST CENTRAL CO. GIVEN POTENTIAL FOR STRONGER STORMS TO AFFECT LINCOLN COUNTY CO...THIS COUNTY HAS BEEN ADDED TO WW 362 BY WFO DENVER/BOULDER.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: TSTM DEVELOPMENT CONTINUES ACROSS WW 362 PER REGIONAL RADAR IMAGERY. TRENDS IN OBJECTIVE ANALYSES SHOW A MODERATE-VERY UNSTABLE AIR MASS AND STRONG BULK SHEAR /35-45 KT PERPENDICULAR TO THE GENERAL N-S INITIATING BOUNDARIES/ INDICATES AN ENVIRONMENT VERY CONDUCIVE FOR SUPERCELL DEVELOPMENT...INCLUDING SPLITTING STORMS. IN ADDITION TO STORMS FORMING ALONG THE FRONT RANGE FROM CO NWD INTO SERN WY...STORMS HAVE ALSO FORMED ALONG THE ERN PERIPHERY OF THE DEN CYCLONE. THE SPECIAL DEN SOUNDING AT 19Z MODIFIED FOR ADDITIONAL SURFACE HEATING AND GREATER MOIST INFLOW /81 F/54 F/ OVER THE LOWER ELEVATIONS REMOVED THE REMAINING CAP AND RESULTED IN VERY STRONG INSTABILITY /MLCAPE 3000+ J PER KG/ FOR STORM DEVELOPMENT OVER THE SRN EXTENT OF WW 362. LOCAL SPC HAIL MODEL SUGGESTS DIAMETERS CAN EXCEED 2 INCH PER THE MODIFIED DEN SOUNDING...WITH THIS VERIFIED BETWEEN 2330-2340Z IN ARAPAHOE COUNTY CO /2.5 INCH/ AND MORGAN COUNTY CO /2.75 INCH/. EFFECTIVE SRH PER OBJECTIVE ANALYSES INDICATED VALUES OF 100-200 M2/S2 EXTENDING FROM ERN WY SSEWD THROUGH ERN CO WITHIN THE CORRIDOR OF ONGOING STORMS. THESE VALUES SHOULD INCREASE THIS EVENING AS SSELY LOW LEVEL WINDS STRENGTHEN INTO ERN CO FURTHER ENHANCING THE TORNADO POTENTIAL. FARTHER S...STORM DEVELOPMENT IS EXPECTED TO REMAIN MORE ISOLATED OVER SERN CO AS THIS REGION REMAINS SOMEWHAT REMOVED FROM STRONGER FORCING FOR ASCENT WITH THE SHORTWAVE TROUGHS SUPPORTING THE ACTIVITY OVER WW 362. HOWEVER...ANY LEFT SPLIT STORMS WILL BE CAPABLE OF MOVING INTO THE SRN EXTENT OF WW 362. ..PETERS.. 06/07/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE SEVERE WEATHER THREAT IS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE BEYOND 02Z WHICH IS THE SCHEDULED EXPIRATION TIME FOR WW 362. IN ADDITION...THE SEVERE WEATHER THREAT SHOULD SPREAD EWD SOME INTO SWRN NEB AND POSSIBLY FAR NWRN KS. THUS...COORDINATION WILL OCCUR SOON WITH AFFECTED WFO/S IN THIS REGION.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: OBJECTIVE ANALYSES INDICATED THE AIR MASS OVER NERN CO INTO NWRN KS AND SWRN NEB REMAINS MODERATELY-STRONGLY UNSTABLE. THIS COMBINED WITH A 30 KT SLY LOW LEVEL JET BENEATH 35 KT WLY MIDLEVEL WINDS MAINTAINING STRONG EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR WILL CONTINUE TO SUPPORT ADDITIONAL ORGANIZED STORMS INCLUDING SUPERCELLS. EFFECTIVE SRH HAS INCREASED TO 200-300 M2/S2 AS EXPECTED AND WILL SUPPORT A CONTINUED POTENTIAL FOR ROTATING STORMS...ESPECIALLY OVER NERN CO. WEAKER LOW LEVEL MOISTURE WITH EWD EXTENT INTO SWRN NEB AND NWRN KS HAVE RESULTED IN HIGHER LCLS /ABOVE 2000 M/ AS COMPARED TO LOCATIONS FARTHER W. OTHERWISE...LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS WILL REMAIN THREATS AS WELL THROUGH THE EVENING. MODELS SUGGEST STORMS MAY EVOLVE INTO AN MCS MOVING ESEWD THROUGH SWRN NEB AND MUCH OF NERN-EAST CENTRAL CO. ..PETERS.. 06/08/2012
